title: Methodus nova et facilis calculum variationum tractandi

deep.reconstruction:
Sections 9-11 set up the first variation of a functional J[y] = ∫ Z(x, y, p, q, r, …) dx, where p = y', q = y'', r = y''' and so on (§7, previous page). The total differential is dZ = M dx + N dy + P dp + Q dq + R dr. Euler stresses that so far the auxiliary variable t plays no role and that the integral is taken with respect to x alone.

The key move, the central idea of E420, is to embed y in a family y(x,t), i.e. to regard y as a function of the two variables x and t. Increasing y by dt·∂y/∂t then gives the 'variation', which is the change in J. In modern terms this is the one-parameter family y(x,ε) with δy = ε·∂y/∂ε|_{ε=0}. Euler explicitly sets t = 0 after differentiating (stated on p. 41).

In §10 he replaces y by y + dt ∂y/∂t inside Z. By §8, Z then changes by dt ∂Z/∂t, so J changes by ∫ dt (∂Z/∂t) dx. Because the integration runs over x only, the constant dt can be taken outside: δJ = dt ∫ (∂Z/∂t) dx. Implicitly this assumes that differentiation in t commutes with integration in x (fixed x-limits).

In §11 he substitutes the expansion from §8. Since dx = 0 under the variation,
δJ = dt ∫ dx [N ∂y/∂t + P ∂²y/∂x∂t + Q ∂³y/∂x²∂t + R ∂⁴y/∂x³∂t + …].
In modern form this is d/dε J[y + εη] = ∫ (Z_y η + Z_{y'} η' + Z_{y''} η'' + …) dx.

The page serves as the preparation for the integration by parts in §13 ff. That step transfers the x-derivatives off ∂y/∂t and yields the Euler–Lagrange equation N − dP/dx + d²Q/dx² − … = 0 together with boundary terms.
errors: No mathematical errors. There are tacit assumptions, standard for the period: the integration limits in x are independent of t, differentiation under the integral sign is allowed, and the mixed partial derivatives commute so that ∂p/∂t = ∂²y/∂x∂t (asserted in §7).

ideas.what: Defining the variation of a functional by embedding the unknown function y(x) in a one-parameter family y(x,t) and differentiating with respect to t (evaluating at t=0)
ideas.modern_name: First variation as the Gateaux/directional derivative d/dε J[y+εη]; one-parameter variations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler, E420 (1771/72), recasting Lagrange's δ-calculus; widely credited to Euler in histories (Goldstine, Fraser)
ideas.where_published: E420 (Novi Comm. Petrop. 16, 1772); also the variational-calculus supplement in Institutiones calculi integralis vol. III (E385)

ideas.what: Taking dt out of the x-integral, i.e. differentiating under the integral sign
ideas.modern_name: Leibniz integral rule with fixed limits
ideas.where_published: Various Euler papers on differentiation under the integral sign (e.g. E44 era work); standard

ideas.what: Expansion of δ∫Z dx in terms of N, P, Q, R times mixed partial derivatives of y
ideas.modern_name: First variation formula for higher-order Lagrangians

deep.surprise_reason: This page is the well-known core of E420's parametric reformulation of the calculus of variations. It is thoroughly discussed in the historical literature and correctly credited to Euler, so nothing here is new.
transcription_corrections: Page number reads '40', not '440' (the extra glyph is a scan artifact).
The first line 'endoque ipsarum' is garbled bleed-through. The text continues from the previous page's 'functio quaecunque' with '…ipsarum x, y, p, q, r etc.'; the first word cannot be read reliably.
